es.summary: Estudia cómo el cuerpo absorbe, distribuye, metaboliza y elimina los fármacos.
key_points: Los cuatro procesos son absorción, distribución, metabolismo y excreción.
La biodisponibilidad indica la fracción del fármaco que llega a la circulación sistémica.
La vida media determina la frecuencia de dosificación.
Factores como edad, embarazo, insuficiencia renal o hepática alteran la farmacocinética.

mechanism: Absorción: paso del fármaco desde el sitio de administración a la sangre.
Distribución: transporte del fármaco a tejidos y órganos, influido por la unión a proteínas.
Metabolismo: transformación hepática (fase I y II) para facilitar la eliminación.
Excreción: eliminación principalmente renal; también biliar, pulmonar o cutánea.
nursing_care: Evaluar función renal (creatinina, diuresis) y hepática (AST, ALT) antes de iniciar terapia.
Monitorear niveles séricos del fármaco cuando exista rango terapéutico definido.
Observar signos de toxicidad o falta de respuesta y notificar al médico.
Retener la dosis si la creatinina está >2 mg/dL o si hay insuficiencia hepática grave.
patient_teaching: Tomar el medicamento exactamente como se indica, sin omitir dosis.
Informar sobre alimentos o suplementos que puedan alterar la absorción.
Reportar cualquier efecto adverso inesperado o cambios en la función renal/hepática.
No compartir el medicamento con otras personas.

outcomes: Mantener niveles séricos del fármaco dentro del rango terapéutico esperado
Demostrar comprensión de los factores que alteran la farmacocinética

interventions.action: Evaluar la función renal y hepática mediante pruebas de laboratorio antes de iniciar el fármaco
interventions.rationale: Permite ajustar la dosis y prevenir acumulación tóxica

interventions.action: Revisar la historia de medicamentos y suplementos del paciente
interventions.rationale: Identifica interacciones que puedan modificar la absorción o el metabolismo

interventions.action: Monitorear signos de toxicidad (náuseas, somnolencia, alteraciones del ritmo cardíaco)
interventions.rationale: Detecta precozmente efectos adversos por acumulación

interventions.action: Educar al paciente sobre la importancia de la adherencia y la toma con alimentos según indicación
interventions.rationale: Optimiza la biodisponibilidad y reduce variabilidad en los niveles plasmáticos

interventions.action: Documentar cualquier cambio en los resultados de laboratorio y comunicar al médico

en.summary: Studies how the body absorbs, distributes, metabolizes, and eliminates drugs.
key_points: The four processes are absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion.
Bioavailability indicates the fraction of the drug that reaches systemic circulation.
Factors such as age, pregnancy, renal or hepatic insufficiency alter pharmacokinetics.

mechanism: Absorption: passage of the drug from the site of administration into the bloodstream.
Distribution: transport of the drug to tissues and organs, influenced by protein binding.
Metabolism: hepatic transformation (Phase I and II) to facilitate elimination.
Excretion: primarily renal elimination; also biliary, pulmonary, or cutaneous.
nursing_care: Assess renal function (creatinine, urine output) and hepatic function (AST, ALT) before initiating therapy.
Monitor serum drug levels when a defined therapeutic range exists.
Observe for signs of toxicity or lack of response and notify the physician.
Hold the dose if creatinine >2 mg/dL or if there is severe hepatic insufficiency.
patient_teaching: Take the medication exactly as directed, without skipping doses.
Inform about foods or supplements that may alter absorption.
Report any unexpected adverse effects or changes in renal/hepatic function.
Do not share the medication with others.

outcomes: Maintain serum drug levels within the expected therapeutic range
Demonstrate understanding of factors that alter pharmacokinetics

interventions.action: Assess renal and hepatic function via laboratory tests before starting the drug
interventions.rationale: Allows dose adjustment and prevents toxic accumulation

interventions.action: Review the patient’s medication and supplement history
interventions.rationale: Identifies interactions that may modify absorption or metabolism

interventions.action: Monitor signs of toxicity (nausea, drowsiness, cardiac rhythm changes)
interventions.rationale: Detects early adverse effects from accumulation

interventions.action: Educate the patient on the importance of adherence and taking with food as directed
interventions.rationale: Optimizes bioavailability and reduces variability in plasma levels

interventions.action: Document any changes in laboratory results and communicate to the physician

sources.name: Pharmacology for Nurses: Pharmacokinetics and Pharmacodynamics

key_points.0.quote: The four primary processes of pharmacokinetics are absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion .

key_points.1.quote: Price and Patel (2022) define bioavailability “for majority purposes” as “the fraction of the active form of a drug that reaches system circulation unaltered.”

key_points.2.quote: Half-life is important because it helps determine the dosing frequency of a medication.

key_points.3.quote: Pregnancy alters the pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetics of each drug and impacts the pregnant body’s response to the drug.

sections.mechanism.0.quote: Absorption refers to the process of a drug traveling from the site of administration, through the body’s membranes, and into the circulating bloodstream.

sections.mechanism.1.quote: Drug distribution refers to the movement of a drug through the body or the way that a drug is spread throughout the body.

sections.mechanism.3.quote: Although the removal of a drug occurs primarily through the renal system, it may also occur through the lungs, skin, bile, or feces.

sections.nursing_care.1.quote: Drug monitoring is sometimes required for drugs with a narrow therapeutic window to ensure that the client’s drug level stays within a safe range.
